newsitem.title: UK: NWE gasoline steady after fire firms U.S. markets.
newsitem.headline: NWE gasoline steady after fire firms U.S. markets.

text.p: NWE gasoline prices were steady on Thursday after a refinery fire lifted U.S. spot markets, but tight aribtrage profitabilty continued to limited trade, traders said.
News that a fire had knocked out a huge catalytic cracking unit at Tosco's Bayway refinery lifted New York Harbor prices by over a cent a gallon and braced European barge and cargo prices.

Interest on both the barge and cargo markets has continued to focus on transatlantic arbitrage with European demand thin, but while there are few prompt cargoes left to move tight freight, space is now limiting the option.
"We've chased the U.S. market lower in its recent falls, so in theory the arbitrage has always been open, but higher freight costs have restricted arbitrage options," a trader at a U.K. major said.
Eurograde barges were assessed around $205/206 a tonne fob ARA and cargoes valued $214.50 cif NWE.
